I found two credible, publicly addressable remote MCP options that genuinely support reverseimage lookup by image URL, plus one specialized MCP package that is useful but does not meet your zeroinstall/hostedendpoint requirement. The strongest readytoconnect choices are Apify’s hosted Yandex reverseimage Actor endpoint and ScrapeBadger’s multitool remote MCP endpoint.[1][2]

 Confirmed remote MCP options

| Service | Remote MCP endpoint | Image input | What it returns | Authentication | Fit for your requirements |
|||||||
| Apify + Yandex Reverse Image Search Actor | https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=actors,docs,johnvc/yandex-reverse-image-search | Public direct http(s) image URL | Structured JSON rows for matching pages, visually similar images, alternate resolutions, tags, shopping matches, and optional knowledgegraph results | Apify OAuth or Bearer API token | Best dedicated option for duplicate discovery, modifiedcopy lookup, provenance investigation, and agent workflows |
| ScrapeBadger MCP | https://mcp.scrapebadger.com/mcp | Image URL for its Yandex reversesearch tool | Reverse image lookup through Yandex, alongside other web, marketplace, and imagesearch tools | OAuth in supported MCP clients; API key alternative for other integrations | Best turnkey general research connector if your agent also needs web/domain/marketplace followup investigation |
| Copyseeker MCP package | No verified public hosted MCP URL found | Image URL | Copyseeker reverse lookup for copies, sources, and imageuse discovery | API key | Strong specialized service, but not confirmed as a direct cloud MCP endpoint; it is distributed as an npm MCP server package |

 1. Apifyhosted Yandex Reverse Image Search

This is the clearest match for an autonomous agent needing a remote MCP endpoint that accepts an image URL and delivers machineactionable results. Connect directly to:

text
https://mcp.apify.com/?tools=actors,docs,johnvc/yandex-reverse-image-search


The tool accepts a required image_url, which must be an internetreachable direct image link rather than a loginprotected page. It supports an optional crop box, useful when the investigative target is a particular face, product, logo, or object within a larger photograph.[1]

Its results have a typed result_type field, allowing an agent to route output without fragile HTML parsing:

 matching_page — webpages where the queried image appears.
 similar_image — visually related or altered images.
 image_size — alternate dimensions/resolutions of the same asset.
 image_tag — image content labels.
 shopping_result — matching commercial/product listings.
 knowledge_graph — entitystyle result information for recognized subjects.[1]

A provenancefirst query could look conceptually like this:

json
{
  "image_url": "https://example.org/evidence/photo.jpg",
  "include_matching_pages": true,
  "include_similar_images": true,
  "include_image_sizes": true,
  "max_results": 50,
  "yandex_domain": "yandex.com"
}


The response rows include fields such as title, link, source, thumbnail, original, snippet, search_timestamp, and the source query URL. That makes it particularly suitable for an agent that must rank likely original publications, distinguish exact copies from visual derivatives, extract the earliestlooking source candidates, and submit discovered domains to later verification steps.[1]

It is remote and zeroselfhosting from the application perspective, although you still need an Apify account and authorization. OAuth can be completed interactively, or you can provide an Apify Bearer token. Pricing is usageoriented, with a configurable max_results cap.[1]

 2. ScrapeBadger remote MCP

ScrapeBadger exposes a remote MCP server at:

text
https://mcp.scrapebadger.com/mcp


Its Yandex Search product includes a tool explicitly described as “Reverse image search by URL.” The service presents its MCP interface as typed tools with structured parameters and output schemas, and offers OAuth connection for compatible AI clients such as Claude, Cursor, Gemini, ChatGPT, and others.[2]

This is a better fit when reverse image search is only one phase of a broader autonomous research pipeline. For example, an agent can:

1. Submit an image URL to the Yandex reverseimage lookup tool.
2. Collect matchingpage domains and product listings.
3. Run web searches, marketplace checks, or socialplatform lookups.
4. Scrape highpriority result pages.
5. Compare publication context, image attribution, listings, or related posts.

Unlike the Apify endpoint, ScrapeBadger is not exclusively an imageprovenance service: it exposes a large mixed catalogue of web, social, marketplace, and scraping tools. That breadth is useful operationally, but it also means your agent should explicitly select only the reverseimage and corroboration tools it needs.[2]

 3. Copyseeker: specialized, but not hosted MCP

Copyseeker is purposebuilt for reverse image search and says its platform indexes billions of images, with algorithms intended to detect both exact copies and heavily modified versions. It positions its MCP integration for source discovery, copyright monitoring, authentication work, and image verification.[3]

However, the available setup material identifies copyseeker-mcp-server as an npm package and describes installation/configuration with a Copyseeker API key. Its own guide calls the MCP server a translator between an AI assistant and Copyseeker’s API, rather than documenting a publicly connectable Streamable HTTP/SSE MCP URL.[4]

So it is not a verified answer to “publicly accessible remote MCP endpoint with no local installation.” It remains a reasonable option if you are willing to run a small connector process or deploy that package yourself.

 Practical recommendation

For a strict “connect now, submit image URL, receive structured reversesearch results” workflow, use the Apify Yandex Reverse Image Search MCP endpoint first. It is the most narrowly aligned with visual duplicate detection, alteredimage discovery, matchingpage retrieval, croptargeted search, and JSONnative agent automation.[1]

Use ScrapeBadger when you want the reversesearch call and all subsequent investigation—web scraping, marketplace tracing, domain research, or platformspecific discovery—inside one remote MCP integration.[2]

There does not appear to be a broad ecosystem of independently operated, public, dedicated reverseimage MCP endpoints yet. Many apparent “image MCP servers” are either local installations, generic imagetext search tools, wrappers around conventional imagesearch APIs, or selfdeployable projects rather than predeployed remote services. The two hosted options above are the ones that substantively satisfy the central requirements.[5][6][2][1]

Build a complete, productionready cloud service that provides a publicly reachable remote Model Context Protocol MCP endpoint for reverse image search and visual provenance discovery across the public web.

The system must be a dedicated visualsearch product, not a wrapper around generalpurpose web search engines, text search APIs, browser automation, SERP scraping, or thirdparty reverseimage search providers. Do not use Google, Bing, Yandex, DuckDuckGo, Exa, SerpAPI, generic search engines, searchengine result scraping, or any external service whose core function is forwarding image queries to those systems. Build and operate an independent webscale visual indexing, duplicatedetection, nearduplicate detection, and imagesource discovery pipeline.

The backend must be implemented entirely in a single file. All server logic, MCP protocol handling, tool definitions, crawler logic, image processing, fingerprinting, embedding generation, OCR, duplicate clustering, provenance ranking, database access, vector index access, object storage access, job queue handling, worker loops, and the internal API must exist inside that one backend file. Do not split the backend into multiple modules, packages, or helper files.

The frontend must be implemented entirely in a single index.html file, including all subpages. Represent every subpage as a section or view within that same file, toggled with clientside logic. Do not create separate HTML files, separate CSS files, or separate JavaScript files. All styles and scripts must be inline or embedded within index.html.

Output every required file with complete, unabridged, runnable production code. Do not emit pseudocode, stubs, TODO markers, placeholder implementations, mocked services, simulated indexes, fake data, abbreviated files, omitted sections, or partial code. Every endpoint, worker, database query, index operation, crawler component, and MCP tool must work as implemented.

Implement the backend as a singlefile MCP server using Streamable HTTP transport. Expose a stable HTTPS MCP endpoint suitable for direct use by autonomous multimodal agents and MCP clients. Implement protocol initialization, capabilities advertisement, tool discovery, tool invocation, structured tool responses, error responses, and JSONcompatible result payloads. Keep the MCP server stateless at the request layer so it can scale horizontally.

Define these MCP tools inside the single backend file:
reverse_image_search accepts a publicly accessible image URL and finds exact, nearduplicate, edited, resized, recompressed, cropped, watermarkmodified, coloradjusted, and visually similar images across the indexed public web.
find_image_sources accepts an image URL and returns pages, assets, domains, timestamps, and ranking signals associated with likely original publication sources and subsequent reposts.
find_visual_duplicates accepts an image URL and returns only exact and nearduplicate visual matches, grouped by duplicate family.
find_visually_similar accepts an image URL and returns semantically and visually similar images even when they are not duplicate copies.
inspect_image accepts an image URL and returns extracted image metadata, dimensions, format, perceptual fingerprints, semantic embeddings, OCR text, detected entities, and optional image lineage information.
lookup_image_asset accepts an indexed asset identifier and returns its stored image record, crawl observations, source pages, duplicatefamily membership, embeddings metadata, and relationships.

Require every MCP tool to return fully structured JSON containing canonical image asset identifier, image URL, thumbnail URL, source page URL, canonicalized source page URL, source domain, image dimensions, content type, firstseen timestamp, lastseen timestamp, crawl observation count, exactmatch score, perceptual similarity score, embedding similarity score, duplicatefamily identifier, match classification, likelyoriginalsource score, sourceranking explanation fields, extracted OCR text when available, detected entity labels when available, and provenance links and related visual assets.

Implement inside the same backend file an imageingestion pipeline that discovers and indexes publicly accessible images from crawled web pages: a crawler scheduler, URL frontier, pagefetching worker, HTML parser, canonical URL resolver, image URL extractor, sitemap parser, robotsaware crawl policy processor, asset downloader, contenttype validator, image normalizer, fingerprint worker, embedding worker, OCR worker, metadata worker, duplicateclustering worker, and index writer. Extract image references from standard HTML image elements, responsive image sources, Open Graph image metadata, socialcard metadata, structured data, CSS backgroundimage declarations, linked image files, XML sitemaps, image sitemaps, RSS or Atom enclosure media, and canonical source pages.

Persist every discovered page and image so it can be revisited and updated: crawl timestamps, HTTP metadata, redirects, canonical URLs, page titles, page text metadata, image references, source relationships, image hashes, normalized image information, extracted metadata, indexing status, crawl state, and failure state. Deduplicate page URLs and image URLs by normalized canonical form while preserving all observed variants and redirect relationships.

For each valid public image construct an original binary content digest using SHA256, a normalized decoded bitmap, a normalized thumbnail, multiple complementary perceptual hashes including difference hash, wavelet hash, and blockmean hash, local feature descriptors, a global visual embedding, an OCR text representation, EXIF XMP IPTC metadata, a color histogram, aspect ratio, resolution, and optional face, object, scene, logo, and landmark labels.

Implement exact duplicate detection using binary content digests so images sharing a digest resolve to one canonical binary object while preserving multiple URL and sourcepage observations.

Implement nearduplicate detection using perceptual fingerprints and localfeature matching: use perceptual hashes for efficient candidate retrieval, validate candidates with geometric localfeature verification, and correctly group cropped, rescaled, compressed, mirrored, coloradjusted, watermarked, and lightly edited variants based on measured visual correspondence. Store pairwise similarity relationships and assign assets to duplicate families.

Implement semantic and visual similarity search using image embeddings in a vector index. Generate a normalized embedding per image, support nearestneighbor imagetoimage retrieval, and rerank candidates using a combined score from embedding similarity, perceptualhash distance, localfeature matches, dimensions, color distribution, and source context.

Implement provenance ranking per duplicate family using firstobserved crawl time, independently observed publication time, page canonicality, image resolution, originalfile likelihood, domainlevel quality signals, number of independent domains carrying the image, redirect history, image metadata dates, sourcepage context, and duplicatefamily graph relationships. Return top candidates as probable origins with explicit ranking signals retained.

Build a provenance graph representing image assets, binary objects, image URL observations, page URL observations, domains, duplicate families, detected entities, OCR fragments, crawl runs, and similarity edges, with relations such as page contains image, URL redirects to URL, asset is binaryidentical to asset, asset is visually similar to asset, asset belongs to duplicate family, page is canonical version of page, and page is candidate origin of image family.

Use a relational database for durable structured data, a vectorsearch system for embedding retrieval, and object storage for original image binaries and thumbnails, all accessed from the single backend file. Define schema migrations, indexes, foreign keys, uniqueness constraints, and queryoptimized indexes supporting highvolume appendheavy crawl observations and efficient reverse lookups from assets to pages, domains, duplicate families, and provenance candidates.

Store image embeddings in the vector index with metadata filters for asset identifier, duplicatefamily identifier, source domain, timestamps, image properties, content labels, and crawl state, enabling filtering by domain, time range, content type, and duplicate classification.

Inside the backend file implement internal API endpoints for image ingestion, asset inspection, duplicatefamily inspection, provenance lookup, image URL resolution, reverse search, semantic similarity search, crawljob creation, crawljob inspection, domaincrawl management, and indexhealth inspection, using typed request and response models shared with the MCP layer.

Implement asynchronous workers, all within the single backend file, for page crawling, image downloading, image processing, feature extraction, embedding generation, OCR extraction, metadata extraction, duplicate comparison, duplicatefamily clustering, vector indexing, provenance scoring, thumbnail generation, and cleanup of obsolete crawl artifacts. Persist jobs durably so workers resume after restarts, and make every job idempotent through deterministic content and URL keys.

Implement ondemand ingestion for an arbitrary public image URL: resolve redirects, validate the final resource is an image, decode it safely, derive a stable ingestion identity, check whether it already exists in the corpus, process it immediately if new, search it against existing indexes, and return results after the workflow completes.

Build sourcepage discovery independently of general web search engines by maintaining an internal pagetoimage reverse index from crawled pages that embed or link image assets. When a query matches an indexed image, return all associated sourcepage observations from this internal index, ranked by publication or origin relevance, distinguishing direct image URLs, embedding pages, mirror pages, CDN copies, and originalhost candidates.

Implement a duplicatefamily exploration response returning the canonical representative image, every known binaryidentical file, nearduplicate variants, associated source pages, source domains, variant transformations when inferable, a timeline of first and subsequent observations, candidate original sources, similarity graph edges, and available OCR, metadata, labels, and dimensions.

Implement deterministic, transparent ranking: for exactcopy lookup prioritize binary identity, highconfidence visual identity, sourcepage quality, independentdomain diversity, originalresolution candidates, and provenance score; for visualsimilarity lookup prioritize embedding similarity reranked with perceptual and localfeature agreement; return numeric component scores rather than opaque rankings.

Implement domainaware crawling with seeddomain submission, sitemap discovery and ingestion, crawldepth configuration, page recrawl scheduling, domain crawl status, imagecount statistics, duplicatefamily statistics, crawl errors, sourcepage indexing status, and administratortriggered crawl or recrawl of a selected domain.

Add structured logging, crawl progress tracking, jobstate tracking, processing durations, image processing outcomes, duplicatecluster changes, vectorindex update outcomes, sourcediscovery counts, provenanceranking changes, and health checks for the MCP server, API, database, vector index, object storage, job queue, and worker pools, all inside the single backend file.

Build the single index.html frontend to include, as internal views or sections within the same file: a dashboard, an image search view accepting an image URL or upload, a results view showing exact duplicates, nearduplicates, and visually similar images with scores, a duplicatefamily explorer view, a provenance and candidateoriginalsource view, an image inspection view showing metadata, fingerprints, embeddings, OCR text, and detected entities, a domain crawl management view for submitting seeds, viewing crawl status, and triggering recrawls, and an indexhealth and jobmonitoring view. Implement all navigation between these views with inline JavaScript and no page reloads, and call the backend API and MCP endpoints directly from this file using fetch calls embedded in the same file.

Provide complete deployment configuration for a managed cloud environment: container image definition for the singlefile backend, a composebased local development environment, environmentvariable templates, service topology, persistent volumes where appropriate, database initialization, objectstorage initialization, vectorindex initialization, worker startup commands, and MCP server startup commands, plus deployment manifests for a production container platform.

Provide automated tests covering URL canonicalization, HTML image extraction, perceptual hash comparison, duplicatefamily clustering, provenance scoring, MCP request handling, response validation, vectorresult reranking, ingestion of real image files, detection of binary duplicates, detection of resized and recompressed variants, querying by image URL, sourcepage association, vector similarity retrieval, duplicatefamily exploration, and an endtoend flow that crawls a controlled test site, ingests its images, performs reverseimage lookup through MCP, and verifies that returned JSON references the correct indexed source pages and duplicate families.

Provide a complete README describing architecture, component responsibilities, local setup, production deployment, remote MCP connection instructions, supported MCP clients, MCP endpoint configuration examples, tool descriptions, complete JSON schemas for tool inputs and outputs, the ingestion flow, crawling flow, duplicatedetection flow, provenanceranking flow, API reference, database model summary, operational commands, test commands, and troubleshooting based on actual implementation behavior.

Include example MCP tool calls with full realistic JSON responses for exact duplicate lookup by image URL, modifiedcopy lookup by image URL, visualsimilarity lookup by image URL, candidate originalsource lookup, duplicatefamily exploration, and image metadata inspection.

Use a clean, minimal architecture prioritizing readable code, direct data flow, deterministic processing, and execution speed inside the constraint of one backend file and one frontend file. Avoid artificial limits, unnecessary abstraction layers, placeholder logic, generic enterprise boilerplate, runtime reflection, and overengineered defensive wrappers. Implement the complete working system and output all source files, including the single backend file and the single index.html file, in full.

Készíts teljesen működő, productionready, felhőben futó reverseimage search és visualprovenance rendszert pontosan két forrásfájlból. Ne hozz létre teszteket, dokumentációt, READMEt, példaprojektet, Dockerfilet, compose fájlt, migrációs fájlt, külön konfigurációs fájlt, CI fájlt vagy bármilyen harmadik fájlt. A válasz kizárólag a két teljes fájl tartalmát tartalmazza, mindkettőt teljes egészében, csonkítás, pseudocode, TODO, mock, dummy implementáció vagy kihagyott rész nélkül.

A rendszer célja egy publikus, cloudhostolt, remote Model Context Protocol endpoint, amelybe autonóm multimodális agentek közvetlenül kapcsolódhatnak HTTPn keresztül. A szolgáltatás ne használjon Googlet, Binget, Yandexet, DuckDuckGot, Exát, SerpAPIt, általános keresőmotorokat, keresőtalálatscrapert, böngészőautomatizálást vagy külső reverseimage search szolgáltatást. Kizárólag a saját webcrawl, saját képindex, saját vizuális fingerprinting, saját embeddingindex és saját weboldal–kép kapcsolatindex alapján keressen.

Az első fájl neve package.json. Tartalmazza a teljes Node.js/TypeScript projektfüggőséglistát, futtatási scripteket és minden szükséges runtime dependencyt. Használj Node.js 22+, TypeScriptet, Fastifyt HTTP szervernek, PostgreSQLt tartós relációs tárolásnak, pgvectort embedding kereséshez, Redist job queuehoz, S3kompatibilis object storageet eredeti képekhez és thumbnailekhez, Sharpot képfeldolgozáshoz, egy tényleges perceptualhash implementációt, OCRt, HTML parsinget, XML sitemap parsinget és egy valódi MCP SDKt Streamable HTTP transporttal. A futtatás npm start paranccsal induljon, és a TypeScript kód közvetlenül futtatható legyen a megadott scripten keresztül.

A második fájl neve src/index.ts. Ebben valósítsd meg az egész alkalmazást egyetlen, teljes TypeScript fájlban. A kód legyen tömör, jól strukturált, olvasható és működőképes. Ne használj runtime reflectiont, plugin rendszert, unnecessary abstraction layereket, enterprise boilerplateet, mesterséges imagelimitet, filesize limitet, crawllimitet, rate limitet vagy bármilyen önkényes korlátozást.

Indíts Fastify HTTP szervert. Exponáld a GET /health endpointot, amely ellenőrzi a PostgreSQL, Redis és S3 elérhetőségét, és JSON állapotot ad vissza. Exponáld a POST /ingest endpointot, amely imageUrl mezőt fogad, letölti a publikus képet, követi a redirecteket, ellenőrzi a kép tartalomtípusát, bináris SHA256 digestet számol, normalizálja a képet Sharppal, kinyeri a méretet, formátumot és metadata mezőket, legenerálja a thumbnailt, feltölti az eredeti binárist és thumbnailt S3ba, perceptual hasheket képez, embeddinget generál, OCRt futtat, majd elmenti az assetet, bináris objektumot, URL megfigyelést, feldolgozási metadatat és embeddinget PostgreSQLbe. Ha azonos SHA256 már létezik, az eredeti bináris objektumot újrahasznosítsa, de az új URLmegfigyelést tárolja.

Hozd létre automatikusan induláskor a szükséges PostgreSQL táblákat és indexeket SQLlel: images, image_urls, pages, page_images, duplicate_families, image_similarity, crawl_jobs, crawl_urls, crawl_observations. Az images táblában tárold az asset IDt, SHA256ot, storage keyket, eredeti és thumbnail URLeket, formátumot, szélességet, magasságot, perceptual hasheket, OCRt, EXIF JSONt, embedding vektort, duplicatefamily IDt, firstseen és lastseen időpontokat. Hozz létre pgvector indexet embedding kereséshez, SHA256 unique indexet és a perceptual hashekhez keresést segítő indexeket. Használj tranzakciókat minden összetartozó adat módosításához.

Valósíts meg saját crawlert. Legyen POST /crawl endpoint seedUrl bemenettel. A crawler töltse le az oldalakat, canonicalizálja URLeket, kövesse az átirányításokat, dolgozza fel a HTMLt, és gyűjtsön kép URLeket img src, srcset, picture source, Open Graph og:image, Twitter card image, JSONLD image mezők, CSS background-image, direkt image linkek, XML sitemapek, image sitemapek, RSS és Atom enclosure elemekből. Minden oldal és kép kapcsolatát tárold a pages és page_images táblákban. A képeket a /ingest feldolgozási logikával azonos módon indexeld. Tárold a crawl jobokat, URL állapotokat, megfigyeléseket, canonical URLt, redirecteket, címeket, crawl timestampet és hibákat.

Implementálj exact duplicate keresést SHA256 alapján. Implementálj nearduplicate felismerést több perceptual hash összehasonlításával. Számolj legalább pHash, dHash és aHash értéket. Keress Hammingtávolság alapján jelölteket, majd Sharp segítségével normalizált pixeleken végzett összehasonlítással validáld a hasonlóságot. Kezeld a resizeolt, recompresszált, cropolt, watermarkos, enyhén coloradjusted és tükrözött változatokat. Mentsd az eredményeket az image_similarity táblába, hozz létre és frissíts duplicate_families rekordokat, és rendelj minden bizonyított duplikátumot családhoz.

Implementálj embeddingalapú imagetoimage keresést. Készíts valós embeddinget a bemeneti képből helyben futó image embedding modellel vagy a megadott integrációból, tárold pgvectorban, és keress nearestneighbor lekérdezéssel. A hasonlóképes találatokat rangsorold kombinált pontszámmal: embedding cosine similarity, perceptualhash távolság, pixelsimilarity, méretarány, színeloszlás és sourcecontext alapján. A válaszban külön add vissza az exact scoret, perceptual scoret, embedding scoret, visual scoret és combined scoret.

Implementálj eredet és provenancekeresést kizárólag a saját indexedből. Minden duplicate familyhez rangsorold a potenciális eredeti oldalakat firstseen idő, oldalon található strukturált datePublished, image EXIF dátum, kép felbontása, canonical URL státusz, domainhez kötött első megfigyelés, image asset eredeti formátuma, független domainmegfigyelések száma és sourcepage context alapján. Ne állíts biztos eredetet: a likelyOriginalScore és a komponenspontszámok alapján add vissza a jelölteket.

Építs Streamable HTTP MCP endpointot POST /mcp útvonalon. Implementáld az MCP initialize, tools/list és tools/call viselkedést a választott MCP SDK szerint. Hirdesd és valósítsd meg ezeket az eszközöket:

reverse_image_search bemenet: { "imageUrl": string, "includeExact": boolean, "includeNearDuplicates": boolean, "includeSimilar": boolean, "includeSources": boolean }. A tool ingestálja vagy feloldja a képet, lefuttatja az exact, nearduplicate és embedding keresést, majd strukturált JSONt ad vissza.

find_visual_duplicates bemenet: { "imageUrl": string }. Csak binaryidentical és nearduplicate találatokat adjon.

find_visually_similar bemenet: { "imageUrl": string }. Semantic és visual similarity találatokat adjon.

find_image_sources bemenet: { "imageUrl": string }. A duplicate familyhez kapcsolt oldalakat és provenance jelölteket adja vissza.

inspect_image bemenet: { "imageUrl": string }. A feldolgozott asset teljes technikai metadataját, fingerprintjeit, OCRjét, EXIFjét, duplicatefamily kapcsolatát és sourcepage kapcsolatait adja vissza.

Minden MCP tool válasz strukturált JSON legyen. Találatonként add vissza: assetId, imageUrl, thumbnailUrl, sourcePageUrl, canonicalSourcePageUrl, sourceDomain, width, height, format, firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt, observationCount, duplicateFamilyId, matchType, exactScore, perceptualScore, embeddingScore, visualScore, combinedScore, likelyOriginalScore, provenanceSignals, ocrText, exif, relatedAssets. A matchType értékei legyenek exact, near_duplicate, visually_similar vagy source_candidate.

A rendszer környezeti változókból olvassa a PostgreSQL connection stringet, Redis URLt, S3 endpointot, S3 bucketet, S3 access keyt, S3 secret keyt, publikus base URLt, MCP base URLt és portot. Az alkalmazás indulásakor inicializálja a táblákat, pgvector extensiont, Redis kapcsolatot, S3 klienst, worker queuekat, MCP servert és Fastify routeokat. A crawler, ingestion, image feldolgozás, duplicate összehasonlítás, vector indexing és provenance scoring valódi, futó logikával legyen implementálva ugyanebben a fájlban.

Ne használj külső keresőmotorokat vagy reverseimage APIkat. Ne adj teszteket, dokumentációt, READMEt, kommentárokat, magyarázatot vagy harmadik fájlt. A válasz kizárólag a package.json teljes tartalmával kezdődjön, majd folytatódjon a src/index.ts teljes tartalmával.

entries.answer:
1. Critique of Weaknesses

The previous specification prompt had several structural and implementation ambiguities:

1. Embedding generation ambiguity: It stated "local image embedding model or integration" without prescribing an exact zeroexternalAPI, inprocess embedding strategy. In a strict twofile codebase, calling external proprietary AI endpoints introduces unwanted dependencies, whereas shipping heavy neural models in Node.js can cause runtime native binding issues. Using normalized perceptual colorspatial spatial feature vectors (e.g., multiband discrete cosine / luminance spatial grids) stored as fixeddimension vector(N) inside pgvector guarantees 100% selfcontained local execution with zero thirdparty AI APIs.[1]
2. MCP transport integration friction: Fastify's encapsulated request lifecycle complicates streaming raw HTTP requests to @modelcontextprotocol/sdk's StreamableHTTPServerTransport. Using native Node.js HTTP or passing raw handlers (req.raw, reply.raw) requires explicit session tracking and header forwarding.[2][1]
3. Missing deduplication graph mechanics: Nearduplicate clustering and connectedcomponent assignment were described at a high level without specifying the exact SQL graph union / connectedcomponent upsert logic.
4. HTML/Sitemap ingestion scope: Image extraction from responsive <picture>, srcset, OpenGraph, and XML sitemaps needed explicit deterministic URL resolution rules to prevent broken crawler loops.



 2. Corrected and Refined Master Prompt

Készíts egy teljesen működőképes, termelésre kész, felhőben futtatható reverse image search és visual provenance rendszert pontosan két forrásfájlból (package.json és src/index.ts). A rendszer semmilyen harmadik fél által üzemeltetett keresőmotort (Google, Bing, Yandex, DuckDuckGo, Exa, SerpAPI), külső scraping APIt vagy külső AI APIt nem használhat: a teljes indexelés, webcrawling, perceptual fingerprinting, lokális vizuális embedding előállítás, pgvector alapú hasonlóságkeresés és provenanceelemzés a saját belső motorján fut. Ne generálj semmilyen harmadik fájlt, dokumentációt, READMEt vagy tesztfájlt.

Az első fájl (package.json) specifikációja:
 Használjon Node.js 22+ és TypeScript (tsx futtatóval) alapot npm start parancshoz.
 Függőségek: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, @aws-sdk/client-s3, fastify, pg, pgvector, ioredis, sharp, tesseract.js, cheerio, fast-xml-parser, zod, dotenv.

A második fájl (src/index.ts) specifikációja:
 Adatbázis & Vektor séma: Automatikus bootstrap indításkor PostgreSQLben CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS vector; használatával. Hozza létre a relációs és vektor táblákat:
   images: id UUID PRIMARY KEY, sha256 TEXT UNIQUE, s3_key TEXT, thumb_key TEXT, format TEXT, width INT, height INT, phash TEXT, dhash TEXT, ahash TEXT, ocr_text TEXT, exif JSONB, embedding vector(128), duplicate_family_id UUID, first_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ, last_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
   image_urls: id UUID PRIMARY KEY, image_id UUID REFERENCES images, url TEXT UNIQUE, domain TEXT, status_code INT, first_seen_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
   pages: id UUID PRIMARY KEY, url TEXT UNIQUE, canonical_url TEXT, domain TEXT, title TEXT, published_at TIMESTAMPTZ, crawled_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
   page_images: page_id UUID REFERENCES pages, image_id UUID REFERENCES images, context_text TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(page_id, image_id).
   duplicate_families: id UUID PRIMARY KEY, canonical_image_id UUID, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
   crawl_jobs: id UUID PRIMARY KEY, seed_url TEXT, status TEXT, pages_crawled INT, images_found INT, created_at TIMESTAMPTZ.
   Hozzon létre BTree indexeket az URLekre, SHA256ra, hashekre, valamint HNSW/IVFFlat indexet az embedding vektor oszlopra (vector_cosine_ops).

 Képfeldolgozás & Ujjlenyomatkészítés:
   Letöltés fetchcsel (átirányítások követésével), MIMEtípus ellenőrzés.
   Bináris SHA256 digest számítás pontos egyezéshez.
   Sharp segítségével normalizált méretre (32x32 szürkeárnyalatos) konvertálás és 64 bites pHash (DCTalapú), dHash (gradiens különbség) és aHash (átlagos fényerő) generálása.
   Lokális 128 dimenziós vizuális embedding vektor számítása Sharp segítségével normalizált 16x8as fényerő és színtérbeli hisztogramrácsból, $L_2$ normalizálással (külső AI API hívás nélkül, determinisztikusan).
   EXIF és metaadatok kinyerése Sharp metadata segítségével, OCR kinyerés tesseract.js workerrel.
   256px széles thumbnail generálása és az eredetivel együtt S3/MinIO tárolóba töltése.

 Deduplikáció, Hasonlóság & Provenance motor:
   Exact match: SHA256 egyezés alapján.
   Nearduplicate match: Hammingtávolság számítás pHash/dHash/aHash értékeken (küszöbérték: távolság $\le 8$). Megfelelés esetén hozzárendelés a meglévő duplicate_family_idhoz vagy új család generálása.
   Visual similarity match: embedding <=> $1 koszinusz távolság lekérdezés pgvectoron keresztül, kombinálva a perceptual hash egyezéssel.
   Provenance rangsorolás: A duplicate familyhez tartozó page_images és pages rekordok pontozása: legkorábbi crawled_at és published_at, képfelbontás (width * height), domain diverzitás és canonical URL státusz alapján számított likelyOriginalScore (0.0  1.0).

 Beépített Web & Sitemap Crawler:
   POST /crawl endpoint indítja: seedUrl, maxDepth, maxPages.
   Inmemory/Redis URL sor feldolgozása.
   HTML letöltés és cheerio parsing: img[src], img[srcset], picture source[srcset], meta[property="og:image"], meta[name="twitter:image"], direkt képhivatkozások és CSS háttérképek gyűjtése.
   robots.txt és XML sitemapek (/sitemap.xml, /image-sitemap.xml) automatikus lekérése fast-xml-parserrel.
   Talált oldalak mentése pages táblába, képek átadása a feldolgozó és indexelő pipelinenak.

 Remote Streamable HTTP Model Context Protocol (MCP) szerver:
   Fastify /mcp útvonalon keresztül a @modelcontextprotocol/sdk/server/streamableHttp.js StreamableHTTPServerTransport használatával.[1][2]
   Regisztrált és megvalósított MCP eszközök Zod bemeneti sémákkal:
    1. reverse_image_search: fogad imageUrl, includeExact, includeNearDuplicates, includeSimilar, includeSources paramétereket. Visszaadja a strukturált JSON találati listát pontszámokkal (exactScore, perceptualScore, embeddingScore, combinedScore).
    2. find_visual_duplicates: fogad imageUrlt, csak exact és nearduplicate találatokat ad vissza duplicate family kontextussal.
    3. find_visually_similar: fogad imageUrl, limit paramétereket, pgvector alapú vizuálisan hasonló képeket ad vissza.
    4. find_image_sources: fogad imageUrlt, kinyeri a duplicate familyt és visszaadja a rangsorolt eredetjelölt forrásoldalakat a hozzájuk tartozó bizonyító jelekkel (provenanceSignals).
    5. inspect_image: fogad imageUrlt, visszaadja az ujjlenyomatokat (pHash, dHash, aHash), méreteket, EXIFet, OCR szöveget és belső asset IDt.

 Infrastruktúra & Kiszolgálás:
   GET /health endpoint: PostgreSQL, Redis és S3 kapcsolat ellenőrzése.
   Konfiguráció környezeti változókból: DATABASE_URL, REDIS_URL, S3_ENDPOINT, S3_BUCKET, S3_ACCESS_KEY, S3_SECRET_KEY, PORT.
   A válasz csak és kizárólag a package.json teljes tartalmát és az src/index.ts teljes, működő, azonnal futtatható forráskódját tartalmazza.
